<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Carrying Value of Foreclosed and Repossessed Assets</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreclosed and repossessed assets are acquired through or instead of loan foreclosure and are initially measured at fair value less estimated costs to sell.&#160; The Company obtains appraisals to determine the initial fair value and then makes any adjustments deemed necessary based on prevailing market conditions and length the asset remains in the Company&#146;s inventory.&#160; Determining the carrying value requires significant management judgment as foreclosed and repossessed assets are typically acquired in distressed situations which may materially impact the valuation compared to similar assets in non-distressed sales transactions.&#160; Also, if foreclosed and repossessed assets are not sold in a timely manner, they can deteriorate in value significantly as there may be volatility in the market.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company had foreclosed and repossessed assets of $4.4 million which, in management&#146;s estimation, were reported at the appropriate carrying value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Tax Assets</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a net deferred tax asset of approximately $242,000. The Company evaluates this asset on a quarterly basis. To the extent the Company believes it is more likely than not that it will not be utilized, the Company will establish a valuation allowance to reduce its carrying amount to the amount it expects to be realized.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, a valuation allowance of $1.1 million has been established against the outstanding deferred tax asset due to incurred net operating losses for state income taxes.&#160; The net operating loss is partially due to YCB&#146;s Nevada subsidiaries that hold and manage YCB&#146;s investments and due to the results of 2009 including elevated provision for loan losses.&#160; The Company is uncertain if it will be able to utilize this benefit, thus a valuation allowance has been established against the state net operating loss.&#160; Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements describes the net deferred tax asset.&#160; The Company has been profitable from 2010 through 2014 and has a positive earnings outlook for 2015.&#160; The net loss for 2009 was primarily attributable to a goodwill and other intangible asset impairment charge of $16.2 million and an elevated provision for loan losses of $15.9 million which were not repeated in subsequent years and are not expected to be repeated in 2015.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company has $682,000 of remaining other intangible assets subject to impairment and has an allowance for loan losses to total loans ratio of 1.07% which management believes is sufficient to cover probable incurred losses as of that date.&#160; The estimate of the realizable amount of this asset is a critical accounting policy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Highlights</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had net income available to common shareholders of $8.6 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to $7.9 million for 2013.&#160; The increase in earnings in 2014 was attributable to increases in net interest income of $1.3 million and a decrease in provision for loan losses of $2.1 million, offset by a decrease in non-interest income of $2.2 million and increases in non-interest expense of $418,000 and income tax expense of $439,000.&#160; Earnings per basic and diluted common shares increased to $2.49 and $2.46, respectively, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to basic and diluted earnings per common share of $2.32 in 2013.&#160; The Company&#146;s book value per common share increased to $20.75 per share at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $17.77 at December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table summarizes selected financial information regarding the Company&#146;s financial performance:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s total assets increased to $888.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $846.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 primarily due to increases in net loans of $44.2 million, securities available for sale of $6.9 million, and deposit for partial redemption of preferred stock and unpaid dividends of $11.3 million, offset by decreases in interest-bearing deposits in other financial institutions of $4.1 million and the settlement receivable for security sales for $11.1 million.&#160; Total liabilities increased $30.8 million as total deposits increased by $7.3 million to $650.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014, primarily due to non-interest deposits increasing by $12.9 million from 2013.&#160; The increase is also attributed to subscription agreement proceeds held in escrow of $20.8 million and other liabilities increasing by $2.5 million to $4.5 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; Total shareholders&#146; equity increased by $11.2 million to $99.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The increase was a result of the Company reporting net income available to common shareholders of $8.6 million and an increase in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) by $3.5 million to $1.8 million, offset by declared and paid dividends on common shares of $1.6 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the second quarter of 2014, the Company announced it had signed an agreement to acquire First Financial Service Corporation (&#147;FFKY&#148;) and its wholly-owned subsidiary, First Federal Savings Bank of Elizabethtown, Kentucky in a stock exchange.&#160; The acquisition was completed on January&nbsp;1, 2015 with the Company acquiring $775.4 million in assets and assuming $743.0 million in liabilities before adjustments for fair value.&#160; The Company issued 792,392 of its common shares with a fair value of $27.20 per share at the exchange date and cash for fractional shares and outstanding options of $431,000 for total consideration of $22.0 million.&#160; Once the transaction closed, the Company redeemed the outstanding preferred shares of FFKY plus the unpaid dividends.&#160; One of the holders of the preferred shares required the Company to put their redemption funds in escrow prior to the end of the year and before the closing.&#160; On December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company wired $11.3 million which was classified on the consolidated balance sheet as &#147;deposit for partial redemption of acquiree&#146;s preferred stock and unpaid dividends&#148;.&#160; Also, during the second quarter of 2014, the Company entered into subscription agreements with private investors to issue 1,120,950 of its common shares to enhance its capital position to effect the acquisition of FFKY.&#160; The Company received proceeds of $20.8 million prior the end of 2014 which was classified on the consolidated balance sheet as &#147;subscription agreement proceeds held in escrow&#148;.&#160; On January&nbsp;1, 2015, the amount of subscription agreement proceeds held in escrow was netted against issuance costs and reclassified to shareholders&#146; equity.&#160; In total, the Company issued 1,913,342 of its common shares to shareholders of FFKY and private investors subsequent to year end.&#160; The acquisition will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s financial statements in 2015.&#160; More information about the redemption of preferred stock and subscription agreement proceeds is provided in footnote 2 &#151; Acquisition Activities in the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Results of Operations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Interest Income</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s principal revenue source is net interest income.&#160; Net interest income is the difference between interest income on interest-earning assets, such as loans and securities, and the interest expense on the liabilities used to fund those assets, such as interest-bearing deposits and borrowings.&#160; Net interest income is impacted by both changes in the amount and composition of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities as well as changes in market interest rates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, net interest income increased $1.3 million, to $32.3 million while the net interest margin on a taxable equivalent basis increased to 4.25% for 2014 from 4.24% in 2013.&#160; The increase in net interest income from 2013 to 2014 was primarily due to an increase in the average balance of loans to $584.1 million in 2014 from $524.8 million in 2013.&#160; The increase in net interest margin was due to a decline in average cost of interest bearing liabilities to 0.34% in 2014 from 0.39%.&#160; The decrease in the cost of interest bearing liabilities was partially offset by a decrease in the yield on interest earning assets of 4 basis points attributable to the decline in the yield on the Company&#146;s investment securities and loan portfolio during 2014.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">29<a name="PB_29_080349_2897"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average interest earning assets increased to $797.3 million in 2014, from $768.5 million in 2013, primarily due to an increase in average total loans while the while the yield declined to 4.96 % from 5.22% over the same period.&#160; The decline in loan yield was due to rate pressure from the maturity and repricing of existing loans in the portfolio.&#160; Additionally, the markets in which the Company competes remain competitive for high quality loans which also places downward pressure on the yield of the loan portfolio.&#160; Loan growth has offset the decline in average yield as the Company has experienced loan growth in its Lexington market through the addition of new lenders.&#160; Also, the yield on loans was positively impacted by an increase in accretion income recognized of $1.0 million in 2014 compared to $623,000 in 2013.&#160; Accretion income was impacted significantly in 2014 by the refinancing of one credit relationship at another financial institution for which the Company had an unamortized discount of $695,000.&#160; The Company does not anticipate a material accretion adjustment related to one credit relationship in 2015, however, accretion income will be impacted by the acquisition of FFKY in 2015.&#160; The Company&#146;s average balance in tax-exempt securities increased from $79.6 million to $80.5 million in 2014, while the yield on a fully taxable equivalent basis declined from 5.77% in 2013 to 5.57% in 2014.&#160; The average balance in taxable securities decreased by $27.6 million to $115.1 million in 2014 while the yield on taxable securities increased to 1.79% in 2014 from 1.74% in 2013.&#160; The decrease in the yield on tax-exempt and taxable securities was due to additional purchases of municipal securities and sales and maturities of higher-yielding mortgage-backed securities during 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average interest bearing liabilities increased to $574.6 million for 2014 from $569.3 million in 2013 with average costs decreasing to 0.34% from 0.39% over the same periods. The decrease in average balance and cost in 2014 was the result of a decline all categories, most significantly in time deposits and other borrowings.&#160; The Company has maintained a strong liquidity position, including securities available-for-sale, which has allowed management to reprice deposits at lower rates at maturity.&#160; As a result, time deposits decreased to an average balance of $141.2 million with an average cost of 0.29% in 2013 from $161.9 million with an average cost of 0.38% in 2013.&#160; Also contributing to the decline in the average cost of funds was a decline in the cost of other borrowings from 1.82% in 2013 to 1.29%.&#160; Other borrowings primarily consist of FHLB advances which the Company has continued to reduce due to its liquidity position and also lower the average cost.&#160; In addition, non-interest bearing deposits increased to an average balance of $188.9 million in 2014 from $172.7 million in 2013 which also improved the Company&#146;s net interest margin.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, net interest income increased to $31.0 million from $28.8 million in 2012 while the net interest margin on a taxable equivalent basis increased to 4.24% from 4.07% during the same period.&#160; The increase in net interest income from 2012 to 2013 is primarily due to a decrease in the Company&#146;s cost of interest bearing liabilities of 31 basis points and an increase in the average balance of non-interest bearing deposits to $172.7 million for 2013.&#160; The decrease in the cost of interest bearing liabilities was partially offset by a decrease in the yield on interest earning assets of 9 basis points attributable to the decline in the yield on the Company&#146;s investment securities and loan portfolio during 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average interest earning assets increased to $768.5 million in 2013, from $741.3 million in 2012, mostly due to increases in average total loans and fees.&#160; The average balance of total loans and fees has increased to $524.8 million in 2013 from $490.0 million in 2012 while the yield declined to 5.22% from 5.43% over the same period.&#160; In April&nbsp;2013, the Company completed the FDIC-assisted acquisition of First Federal Bank in Lexington, Kentucky which resulted in the addition of loans with a net carrying value of $63.6 million.&#160; The acquired portfolio consisted primarily of fixed rate, one-to-four family loans.&#160; Interest income on loans was bolstered by the recognition of $623,000 of accretion during 2013 from the loans acquired as part of the First Federal transaction.&#160; The decline in loan yield was due to the continued downward pressure resulting from competition in the Company&#146;s market.&#160; Overall, loan demand remains soft as the Company continues to generate the significant portion of its originations from refinancing the debt of customers at other institutions.&#160; The Company also faces pressure to lower rates for existing customers or risk losing them to competitors.&#160; The Company&#146;s average balance in tax-exempt securities increased from $72.0 million to $79.6 million in 2013, while the yield on a fully taxable equivalent basis declined from 6.09% in 2012 to 5.77% in 2013.&#160; The average balance in taxable securities decreased by $9.7 million to $142.7 million in 2013 while the yield on taxable securities decreased to 1.74% in 2013 from 1.94% in 2012.&#160; The decrease in the yield on tax-exempt and taxable securities was due to additional purchases of municipal securities and sales and maturities of higher-yielding mortgage-backed securities during 2013.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average interest bearing liabilities decreased to $569.3 million for 2013 from $574.8 million in 2012 with average costs decreasing to 0.39% from 0.70% over the same periods. The decrease in average balance and cost in 2013 was the result of a decline all categories, most significantly in time deposits, other borrowings, and short-term borrowings.&#160; The Company continues to maintain a strong liquidity position, including securities available-for-sale, which has allowed management to reprice deposits at lower rates at maturity or as market conditions dictate.&#160; In addition, non-interest bearing deposits increased to an average balance of $172.7 million in 2013 from $141.3 million in 2012 which also improved the Company&#146;s funding mix.&#160; As a result, time deposits decreased to an average balance of $161.9 million with an average cost of 0.38% in 2013 from $191.7 million with an average cost of 0.74% in 2012.&#160; Also contributing to the decrease in cost of funds was a reduction in the average cost of short-term borrowings which declined to 0.25% in 2013 from 1.15% in 2012, resulting in a decline in interest expense recognized of $493,000 to $113,000 in 2013.&#160; The decline was attributable to the maturation of a structured repurchase agreement in late 2012 that had a balance of $9.8 million at a rate of 4.97%.&#160; Also contributing to the decrease in cost of funds, was a shift in deposit mix from higher costing time deposits to lower costing savings and other transaction accounts which had an average balance $311.7 million in 2013 compared to $263.4 million in 2012 with average costs of 0.19% and 0.27% over the same periods, respectively.&#160; In addition, the Company lowered its interest expense associated with other borrowings by $370,000 with approximately $63.0 million in new advances at lower rates and repayment of $57.4 million during 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Table 3 illustrates the extent to which changes in interest rates on a fully taxable equivalent basis and changes in the volume of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities affected the Company&#146;s interest income and interest expense during the periods indicated.&#160; Information is provided in each category with respect to (i)&nbsp;changes attributable to changes in volume (changes in volume multiplied by prior rate), (ii)&nbsp;changes attributable to changes in rate (changes in rate multiplied by prior volume), and (iii)&nbsp;the net change.&#160; The changes attributable to the combined impact of volume and rate have been allocated proportionately to the changes due to volume and the changes due to rate.&#160; A tax rate of 34% was used in adjusting interest on tax-exempt assets to a fully taxable equivalent (&#147;FTE&#148;) basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-interest Income</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-interest income was $6.4 million for 2014, $8.7 million for 2013, and $8.4 million for 2012.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, non-interest income decreased by 25.8% as compared to 2013 due primarily to the $1.9 million bargain purchase gain which was not repeated in 2014 and decreases in net gain on sale of available for sale securities of $274,000 and mortgage banking income of $91,000 offset by an increase in interchange income of $76,000.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, non-interest income increased by 3.1% as compared to 2012 due primarily to the recognition of a bargain purchase gain of $1.9 million and an increase in interchange income of $54,000, offset by decreases net gain on sale of available for sale securities of $1.4 million and mortgage banking income of $204,000.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">33<a name="PB_33_073159_7748"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">* Not meaningful</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012 service charges on deposit accounts remained flat at $3.4 million.&#160; The majority of service fees earned were non-sufficient funds and overdraft fees, which contributed $1.9 million to service charges recognized in 2014 and 2013.&#160; Also contributing to service fee income in 2014 and 2013, were monthly service fees on checking accounts of $797,000 and $795,000, respectively, and ATM surcharge fees of $257,000 and $284,000, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2014, the Company received net proceeds of $43.7 million on sales of available for sale securities for net gains of $468,000 compared to proceeds of $51.0 million and net gains of $742,000 million in 2013.&#160; The proceeds from sales are reinvested in the security portfolio as management continues to selectively sell securities when it is determined a change in the prepayment risk may reduce the unrealized gain in an investment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, mortgage banking income decreased to $126,000 from $217,000 in 2013 and $421,000 in 2012.&#160; In 2014, the Company sold $4.8 million of loans into the secondary market compared to $10.3 million in 2013 and $20.8 million in 2012.&#160; During 2013, management elected to retain a higher percentage of its mortgage loans in the portfolio rather than selling into the secondary market to bolster the loan portfolio and increase interest income which has led to an increase in the loan portfolio but declining mortgage banking income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Earnings on company owned life insurance decreased slightly by $6,000 to $672,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 as compared to $678,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013. In 2014, crediting rates remained flat causing only a slight change in income.&#160; During 2013, earnings on company owned life insurance decreased slightly by $19,000 to $678,000 from $697,000 for the equivalent period in 2012 as the crediting rate declined slightly from 2012.&#160; The Company did not purchase additional company owned life insurance policies during 2014, 2013, or 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2014, interchange income increased to $1.2 million from $1.1 million in 2013.&#160; The Company continues to focus on increasing interchange income through various initiatives including offering incentives to current and new customers.&#160; In 2013, interchange income increased to $1.1 million from $1.0 million in 2012.&#160; The Company added new deposit accounts during 2013 and 2012 which also factored into the increase in interchange income over the respective periods.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-interest Expense</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-interest expense increased to $26.5 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $26.1 million in 2013 due to increases in salaries and employee benefits, occupancy, and legal and professional, offset by decreases in data processing, foreclosed and repossessed assets, and other expenses.&#160; In 2013, non-interest expense increased to $26.1 million from $23.7 million for the same period in 2012 due to increases in salaries and employee benefits, equipment, data processing, legal and professional, and other expense, offset by a decrease in foreclosed and repossessed assets, net.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaries and employee benefits increased $497,000, to $13.9 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The increase is attributable to the rise in full time equivalent employees (&#147;FTE&#148;) to 210 from 204 in 2013.&#160; The average expense per FTE remained at $66,000 for 2014 and 2013, as employee group insurance increased by $55,000 and performance based compensation (including stock based compensation) increased by $127,000 for the year.&#160; As the Company continues to increase net income and meet budgetary goals, compensation based on performance has also increased.&#160; Additionally, the Company added staff during 2014 to prepare for the acquisition and integration of FFKY which also contributed to the increase in expense and the number of FTE&#146;s in 2014.&#160; In 2013, salaries and employee benefits increased to $13.4 million from $12.1 million in 2012 with an increase in the number of full time equivalent employees (&#147;FTE&#148;) to 204 at the end of 2013 from 197 at December&nbsp;31, 2012, which was attributed to the First Federal FDIC-assisted transaction in April&nbsp;2013.&#160; The average expense per FTE increased to $66,000 from $62,000 in 2013 and 2012, respectively, as employee group insurance increased by $183,000 and performance based compensation (including stock based compensation) increased by $45,000 for the year.&#160; Also factoring into the increase in salaries and benefits during 2013 were retention bonuses paid to staff of First Federal to work through the conversion of data to the Company&#146;s core processor and overtime and bonuses to staff in assisting with the conversion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Occupancy expense increased by $282,000 to $2.5 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 compared to the prior year.&#160; A majority of the increase was the result of branches acquired in the 2013 FDIC-assisted transaction of First Federal Bank of Lexington, Kentucky as expense was recognized for twelve months in 2014 compared to eight months in 2013.&#160; Three branches were acquired as part of the transaction, two of which were purchased and one in which the lease was assumed.&#160; Occupancy expense increased slightly by $50,000 to $2.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to the same period in 2012.&#160; Increases in office building depreciation of $114,000, repairs and maintenance of $112,000 and rent of $156,000 were offset by an increase in rental income of $305,000.&#160; The increase was attributable to the new branches acquired and the rental income as a portion of the branch space was leased to third-parties.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equipment expense remained flat at $1.3 million in 2014 compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 as decreases in repairs and maintenance were fully offset by increases in depreciation expense for computer hardware and software.&#160; The Company has continued to focus on utilizing software to leverage resources and improve efficiency resulting in additional deprecation.&#160; In 2013, equipment expense increased to $1.3 million compared to $1.1 million compared to 2012, which was attributable to increases in repairs and maintenance and depreciation expense for computer equipment.&#160; During 2013, the Company incurred equipment expense associated with the acquisition of First Federal including the replacement of existing computer hardware and software and general repairs and maintenance.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, data processing expense decreased by $177,000 to $2.6 million, compared to $2.8 million for the same period in 2013.&#160; The decrease is attributed to the conversion of First Federal to the Company&#146;s core data processor and communication expenditures to connect the new branches to our network in 2013 that was not repeated in 2014.&#160; Data processing expense increased in 2013 by $528,000 to $2.8 million, compared to $2.3 million for the same period in 2012.&#160; The increase is attributed to increases in data processing services of $189,000, third party core data processor expense of $207,000, and communication lines of $107,000 associated with the First Federal conversion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal and professional service fees increased by $458,000 to $2.5 million in 2014 compared to $2.0 million in 2013 primarily due to legal and consulting fees associated with the acquisition of FFKY including preparation and negotiation of the merger and share exchange agreement and preparation and review of applicable regulatory filings.&#160; The Company recognized increases in legal fees of $409,000 and audit and accounting services of $91,000 compared to 2013.&#160; In 2013, legal and professional service fees increased by $312,000 to $2.0 million compared to $1.7 million in 2012.&#160; The increase was due to higher professional services expense of $187,000, legal fees of $103,000 and audit and accounting services of $58,000, offset by a decrease in legal fees for loans of $24,000.&#160; During 2013, the Company incurred additional professional service fees, including accounting and auditing, associated with the acquisition of First Federal of Lexington, Kentucky including valuations of acquired loans and deposits and audit, legal, and investment banker fees.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreclosed and repossessed assets expense, net, decreased to $162,000 for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $644,000 in 2013 due primarily to net gains on sales of $350,000 in 2014 compared to net losses on sales of $265,000 in 2013, offset by an increase in expense on other real estate owned of $244,000.&#160; During 2014, the Company realized a gain of $527,000 on the disposition of one property; there were no properties disposed in 2013 with gains recognized greater than $50,000.&#160; Additionally, the Company recognized income from foreclosed and repossessed assets of $138,000 in 2014 compared to $25,000 in 2013.&#160; The company has one property that accounted for the majority of rental income recognized in 2014.&#160; Foreclosed and repossessed assets expense, net, decreased to $644,000 for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 from $1.1 million in 2013 due primarily to decreases in net losses on sales of $265,000 and decreased expense of other real estate owned of $260,000.&#160; The decrease in net losses on sales of foreclosed and repossessed assets was due to a decrease in sales (both cash and financed) as well as smaller incurred net losses per property sold as compared to 2012.&#160; During 2012, the Company recognized a combined loss of $359,000 on the disposition of two properties.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, other expenses decreased by $125,000 to $2.6 million from $2.7 million over the same period in 2013.&#160; The decrease is primarily due to a reduction in telephone expense of $98,000 and losses on sales of fixed assets of $93,000.&#160; During 2013, the Company sold, at a $99,000 loss, a property that had been held for possible branch expansion as compared to recognized losses of $6,000 in 2014.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, other expenses increased by $440,000 to $2.7 million from $2.3 million over the same period in 2012.&#160; The increase is attributed to a loss on sale of fixed assets and increased core deposit intangible amortization.&#160; As part of the First Federal of Lexington, Kentucky acquisition, the Company recorded a core deposit intangible asset of $668,000 which increased the amount of amortization recognized during the year.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Income Tax Expense</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s income tax increased to $2.0 from $1.6 million in 2013 while the effective tax rate also increased to 18.2% from 15.3% over the same period, respectively.&#160; The increase in income tax expense and effective tax rate in 2014 was attributable to non-deductible expenses of $659,000 incurred during 2014 for the acquisition of FFKY.&#160; Income tax expense for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 was $1.6 million compared to $1.7 million in 2012 while the effective tax rate decreased to 15.3% from 18.0% over the same period.&#160; The decrease in income tax expense and effective tax rate was attributable to the formation of the Company&#146;s captive insurance subsidiary, CBIN Insurance,&nbsp;Inc. during the fourth quarter of 2012.&#160; CBIN Insurance,&nbsp;Inc. issued insurance policies to the Company&#146;s subsidiaries effective beginning in 2013 for certain gaps in coverage and insurable risks that may not be cost effectively obtained through third parties.&#160; From an income tax perspective, CBIN Insurance,&nbsp;Inc.&#146;s revenue is exempt from income taxes up to $1.2 million while the expense at the subsidiaries is tax deductible.&#160; As a result, the Company realized a tax benefits of $384,000 in 2014 and $375,000 during 2013.&#160; Also impacting the Company&#146;s effective tax rate in 2013 was an increase in tax-exempt income of $74,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial Condition</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Loan Portfolio</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s loan portfolio increased to $603.6 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $560.9 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; All categories of loans increased from the previous year with exception of consumer loans, which declined by $122,000.&#160; The largest increases occurred in the Company&#146;s commercial real estate and commercial loan portfolios of $14.6 million and $16.3 million, respectively.&#160; Also impacting the loan portfolio during 2014 were charge-offs of $3.4 million and loans transferred into other real estate owned of $1.6 million.&#160; During 2014, the Company recorded originations, net of payments, of $44.7 million as the Company saw an increase in loan demand in addition to retaining more mortgage loans in the portfolio as opposed to selling into the secondary market.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commercial loans, which consist of loans to business customers secured by business assets such as accounts receivable, inventory, and equipment, had the largest increase to $123.7 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $107.5 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase in the commercial portfolio was mostly due to the addition of new commercial lenders to the Company, particularly in the Lexington, Kentucky market, and continued organic growth in the other markets in which it operates.&#160; Commercial loans have certain inherent risks which require loan officers to carefully monitor the borrower&#146;s financial condition and receive periodic updates on the aging and balance of accounts receivable and inventory, if secured by these types of assets.&#160; Should the Company be forced to pursue foreclosure, there can often be significant erosion in the value of the collateral securing these types of loans.&#160; The value of equipment securing commercial borrowings generally tends to depreciate in value rapidly and/or may be industry specific with a limited market for resale.&#160; Accounts receivable are most likely have significant past due issues if the borrower is having financial difficulty and also may be worth a fraction of the balance while inventory may be stale.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Construction loans increased by $2.9 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 to $42.8 million.&#160; Demand for construction loans has increased compared to declines in 2009 through 2012, however, the Company remains selective in its growth in this area due to the amount of charge-offs incurred in the most recent economic downturn.&#160; Construction loans consist of both individual and business borrowings for the development and construction of 1-4 family residences and subdivisions.&#160; The repayment of commercial construction loans is dependent on the resale to third parties in a timely fashion.&#160; Should there be a significant delay in selling the finished properties or a downturn in the market, the developer may not receive cash sufficient to service their borrowings.&#160; In addition, if the Company forecloses on a partially or fully developed property, there can be significant erosion in value as the improvements may have deteriorated resulting in losses to the Company.&#160; Management has continued to work with our construction borrowers who are having difficulty to minimize our loss exposure and prevent foreclosure including restructuring where appropriate.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">37<a name="PB_37_073159_7091"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commercial real estate loans increased $14.6 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 to $213.0 million from $198.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; During 2014 the Company continued to increase it commercial real estate loan portfolio through its expansion into Lexington, Kentucky in 2013 and the hiring of new commercial loan officers.&#160; There continues to remain strong competition from other financial institutions in our market for new commercial real estate loans to qualified customers and, in some cases, we have declined to match offering rates that we believed were not commensurate with the associated risk.&#160; Commercial real estate loans are secured by owner occupied properties and commercial properties rented to third parties.&#160; Commercial real estate loans secured by owner occupied properties are dependent upon the profitability of the underlying business for repayment.&#160; Typically, commercial real estate loans secured with owner occupied property have a lower risk of loss compared to other types of commercial real estate as evidenced by the Company&#146;s loss history.&#160; Commercial real estate secured by non owner occupied properties are considered to be higher risk as the repayment is dependent upon some form of rental income.&#160; Generally, loans in this category are secured by multi-tenant properties leased to retail and commercial customers and hotels/motels.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Residential real estate loans increased from $209.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 to $218.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014, an increase of $9.1 million.&#160; Residential loans included borrowings secured by first and second liens on 1-4 family residential properties, including home equity lines of credit.&#160; The Company retained a higher percentage of its originated residential real estate loans in 2014 as opposed to selling into the secondary market.&#160; As a result, loans sold during 2014 declined to $4.8 million from $10.3 million in 2013 while outstanding residential real estate loans increased over the same period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s lending activities remain primarily concentrated within its existing markets, and are principally comprised of loans secured by single-family residential housing developments, owner occupied manufacturing and retail facilities, general business assets, and single-family residential real estate.&#160; The Company emphasizes the acquisition of deposit relationships from new and existing commercial business and real estate loan clients.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Table 6 provides a breakdown of the Company&#146;s loans by type during the past five years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Allowance and Provision for Loan Losses</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal regulations require insured institutions to classify their assets on a regular basis.&#160; The regulations provide for three categories of classified loans:&#160; substandard, doubtful and loss.&#160; The regulations also contain a special mention and a specific allowance category.&#160; Special mention is defined as loans that do not currently expose an insured institution to a sufficient degree of risk to warrant classification but do possess credit deficiencies or potential weaknesses deserving management&#146;s close attention.&#160; Assets classified as substandard or doubtful require the institution to establish general allowances for loan losses.&#160; If an asset or portion thereof is classified as loss, the insured institution must either establish specified allowances for loan losses in the amount of 100% of the portion of the asset classified loss, or charge off such amount.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">39<a name="PB_39_073951_563"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>
</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='39',FILE='C:\JMS\C901944\14-26402-1\task7277097\26402-1-bq.htm',USER='C901944',CD='Mar 16 20:04 2015' -->

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains the allowance for loan losses at a level that is sufficient to absorb probable credit losses incurred in its loan portfolio.&#160; The allowance is determined based on the application of loss estimates to graded loans by categories.&#160; Management determines the level of the allowance for loan losses based on its evaluation of the collectability of the loan portfolio, including the composition of the portfolio, historical loan loss experience, specific impaired loans, and general economic conditions.&#160; Allowances for impaired loans are generally determined based on collateral values or the present value of estimated future cash flows.&#160; The allowance for loan losses is increased by a provision for loan losses, which is charged to expense, and reduced by charge-offs of specific loans, net of recoveries.&#160; Changes in the allowance relating to impaired loans are charged or credited directly to the provision for loan losses.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s allowance for loan losses totaled $6.5 million, a decrease of $1.5 million from December&nbsp;31, 2013 which lowered the allowance for loan losses to total loans ratio to 1.07% from 1.43% for the same periods, respectively while net charge-offs decreased by $1.3 million to $2.8 million in 2014.&#160; The Company had lower charge-offs in all loan categories with the exception of Commercial loans which increased to $910,000 for 2014 compared to $132,000 in 2013.&#160; The decrease in total charge-offs was primarily due to a reduction in construction charge-offs as the Company recorded a $2.0 million charge-off for one credit relationship in 2013.&#160;&#160; The reduction in the Company&#146;s allowance is the result of improving credit quality conditions in its portfolio.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s impaired loans were $16.6 million as compared to $19.8 million.&#160; The same improving credit trend was present in both total past due and non-accrual loans which declined to $12.1 million and $7.5 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, respectively, from $16.4 million and $7.8 million at the end of 2013.&#160;&#160; In addition, the Company has continued to experience declining net charge-offs which has reduced the allocation for loans collectively evaluated for impairment.&#160; Commercial loans have been particularly impacted by the overall decline in net charge-offs in its portfolio as the allowance for loan losses allocated declined to $970,000 as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $1.8 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; Of the total allowance allocated for Commercial loans, the majority was for loans collectively evaluated for impairment, or $905,000 which is based on average three year net charge-offs, adjusted for qualitative factors.&#160; Management has allocated amounts for probable incurred losses in the Company&#146;s loan portfolio based on the best estimate available as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As previously noted, the Company completed its acquisition on January&nbsp;1, 2015 of First Financial Service Corporation (&#147;FFKY&#148;).&#160; At the time of acquisition, FFKY had a substantial amount of past due, non-accrual, and classified credits which will materially impact the Company&#146;s credit quality ratios in 2015.&#160; The Company is currently in the process of determining the fair value of the loan portfolio, including the amount of discount to apply to the purchased credit impaired loans.&#160; Purchased credit impaired loans do not have an allowance for loan losses allocated to them unless there is a subsequent deterioration in expected cash flows subsequent to the acquisition.&#160; As such, the amount of allowance for loan losses as a percentage of total loans will be significantly lower in 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Provisions for loan losses are charged against earnings to maintain the allowance for loan losses at the appropriate level and is based on historical experience, the volume and type of lending conducted by the Company, the status of past due principal and interest payments, general economic conditions, and inherent credit risk related to the collectability of the Company&#146;s loan portfolio.&#160; The provision for loan losses decreased to $1.3 million for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $3.4 million for the same period in 2013, or $2.1 million and 62.6%.&#160; During 2014, the volume of problem credits decreased as compared to 2013 which resulted in lower non-performing loans of $7.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 as compared to $7.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; Over the same period, classified loans (includes loans classified as substandard and doubtful) decreased to $15.7 million as compared to $19.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 (see Footnote 4 to the Company&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements for further information on classified loans).&#160; During 2014, the number of new identified classified credits continued to slow while the Company was able to resolve previously identified classified credits through foreclosure or improvement by the borrower.&#160; Also contributing to the decrease in provision from 2013 to 2014 was provision of $2.0 million on one construction loan compared to $361,000 for the same credit in 2014.&#160; During 2014, the Company determined there was additional exposure as the legal proceedings moved forward.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the loan has a carrying amount of $453,000 without a recorded allowance and is included in the Company&#146;s non-accrual and classified loan totals as of the same date.&#160; Excluding the aforementioned credit, the Company has continued to see improvement in credit quality as evidenced by improvements in both non-accrual and classified loans.&#160; As previously noted, the Company&#146;s acquisition of FFKY is expected to significantly increase past due, non-accrual, and classified loans but it is not anticipated the acquisition will materially impact provision for loan losses in the immediate future.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">40<a name="PB_40_073951_9497"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table depicts management&#146;s allocation of the allowance for loan losses by loan type during the last five years.&#160; Allowance funding and allocation is based on management&#146;s assessment of economic conditions, past loss experience, loan volume, past-due history and other factors. Since these factors and management&#146;s assumptions are subject to change, the allocation is not necessarily indicative of future loan portfolio performance.&#160; Allocations of the allowance may be made for specific loans or loan categories, but the entire allowance is available for any loan that may be charged off.&#160; Loan losses are charged against the allowance when a loss has been confirmed by management.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Asset Quality</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans, including impaired loans, are placed on non-accrual status when they become past due 90 days or more as to principal or interest.&#160; When loans are placed on non-accrual status, all unpaid accrued interest is reversed.&#160; These loans remain on non-accrual status until the loan becomes current or the loan is deemed uncollectible and is charged off.&#160; The Company defines impaired loans to be those loans that management has determined it is probable, based on current information and events, the Company will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160; Loans individually classified as impaired decreased to $16.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $19.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; Impaired loans at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 included $11.9 million and $10.5 million, respectively, of troubled debt restructurings (&#147;TDR&#146;s&#148;).&#160; For further information on non-performing loans and their impact on the Company&#146;s earnings, see discussion above under &#147;Allowance and Provision for Loan Losses&#148;.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total non-performing loans decreased to $7.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $7.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 with total non-performing assets decreasing to $12.0 million from $13.8 million as of the same dates, respectively.&#160; Non-performing assets also include foreclosed real estate and other repossessed assets that have been acquired through foreclosure or acceptance of a deed in lieu of foreclosure.&#160; Foreclosed real estate and repossessed assets are carried at fair value less estimated selling costs, and are actively marketed for sale.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Table 10 provides the Company&#146;s non-performing loan experience during the past five years.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities available for sale increased to $202.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $195.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase in available for sale securities was due primarily to purchases of $50.0 million, offset by sales of $43.7 million and maturities, prepayments and calls of $15.9 million during 2014.&#160; The current strategy for the securities portfolio is to maintain an intermediate average life that remains relatively stable in a changing interest rate environment, thus minimizing exposure to sustained increases in interest rates.&#160; The investment portfolio primarily consists of mortgage-backed securities, securities issued by the United States government and its agencies, securities issued by states and municipalities, and trust preferred securities.&#160; Mortgage-backed securities consist primarily of obligations insured or guaranteed by Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, Federal National Mortgage Association, or Government National Mortgage Association.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Deposits</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company attracts deposits from the market areas it serves by offering a wide range of deposit accounts with a variety of rate structures and terms.&#160; The Company uses interest rate risk simulations to assist management in monitoring the Company&#146;s deposit pricing, and periodically may offer special rates on certificates of deposits and money market accounts to maintain sufficient liquidity levels.&#160; The Company relies primarily on its retail and commercial sales staff and current customer relationships to attract and retain deposits.&#160; Market interest rates and competitive pressures can significantly affect the Company&#146;s ability to attract and retain deposits.&#160; The Company&#146;s strategic plan includes continuing to grow non-interest bearing accounts which contribute to higher levels of non-interest income and net interest margin.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total deposits increased by $7.3 million to $650.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 due mainly to an increase in non-interest bearing deposits of $12.9 million.&#160; Total interest bearing deposits decreased by $5.6 million with decreases in total certificates of deposits of $16.8 million, offset by increases in demand accounts of $2.6 million, money markets of $4.7 million, and savings of $4.0 million.&#160; In 2014, management continued its focus on repricing maturing certificates of deposits and lowering the current offering rates for other interest bearing deposit accounts given the current rate environment.&#160; The Company was able to reprice deposits rates at or below rates offered in its markets and was able to lower the average rate for all interest-bearing deposit accounts to 0.22% in 2014 from 0.25% in 2013.&#160; As a result of the reduction in rates, the Company saw a decrease in its certificate of deposit accounts.&#160; The Company&#146;s non-interest bearing deposits increased in 2014 due to an emphasis on growing these types of accounts through allocating a significant portion of incentive based compensation for business service and retail employees on growth of non-interest deposits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Table 13 provides a profile of the Company&#146;s deposits during the past five years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Short-Term Borrowings</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s short-term borrowings consist of repurchase agreements and federal funds purchased, which represent overnight liabilities to non-affiliated financial institutions.&#160; While repurchase agreements are effectively deposit equivalents, these arrangements consist of securities that are sold to commercial customers under agreements to repurchase.&#160; Short-term borrowings increased slightly to $45.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $45.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 due to an increase in federal fund purchased of $5.5 million offset by a decrease in repurchase agreements of $5.3 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Other Borrowings</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other borrowings totaled $67.0 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 and consist of FHLB advances, Subordinated Debentures, and a holding company term loan. During 2014, the Company borrowed $10.0 million at the holding company and contributed the proceeds to its subsidiary, Your Community Bank, to enhance capital for the FFKY acquisition and merger. The increase in the term loan was offset by a decrease in FHLB advances of $10.0 million.&#160; Management evaluates its use of wholesale funding in relation to its other funding options (deposits, federal funds purchased, sales of securities,&nbsp;etc.) based on the cost and the Company&#146;s immediate and long-term liquidity needs (see the &#147;Liquidity&#148; section for further information on FHLB advance availability).</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity levels are adjusted in order to meet funding needs for deposit outflows, repayment of borrowings, and loan commitments and to meet asset/liability objectives.&#160; The Bank&#146;s primary sources of funds are deposits; repayment of loans and mortgage-backed securities; Federal Home Loan Bank advances; maturities of investment securities and other short-term investments; and income from operations. While scheduled loan and mortgage-backed security repayments are a relatively predictable source of funds, deposit flows and loan and mortgage-backed security prepayments are greatly influenced by general interest rates, economic conditions and competition.&#160; Liquidity management is both a daily and long term function of business management.&#160; If the Banks require funds beyond those generated internally, then as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 the Banks had $61.4 million in additional capacity under its borrowing agreements with the FHLB based on the Banks&#146; current FHLB stock holdings and approximately $32.0 million in federal funds purchased with other financial institutions.&#160; The holding company&#146;s primary source of liquidity is dividends from its subsidiaries, YCB and SCSB which are limited by banking regulations.&#160; Currently, YCB can declare and pay dividends of $2.5 million while SCSB cannot declare dividends without prior regulatory approval.&#160; The Company anticipates it will have sufficient funds available to meet current loan commitments and other credit commitments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Capital</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total capital of the Company increased to $99.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $88.3 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013, an increase of $11.2 million or 12.7%.&#160; The increase in capital was primarily due to net income available to common shareholders of $8.6 million offset by dividends on common shares of $1.6 million and the growth in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) by $3.5 million to $1.8 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; We are prohibited from paying dividends on our common stock unless we have fully paid all required dividends on the senior preferred stock.&#160; To date we have met all our required dividend payments on the senior preferred stock and thus are not prohibited from paying dividends on our common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has been repurchasing shares of its common stock since May&nbsp;21, 1999.&#160; A net total of 416,111 shares at an aggregate cost of $7.2 million have been repurchased since that time under both the current and prior repurchase plans.&#160; The Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase plan in June&nbsp;2007 under which a maximum of $5.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock could be purchased.&#160; Through December&nbsp;31, 2014, a total of $1.6 million had been expended to purchase 85,098 shares under this plan.&#160; The Company&#146;s ability to repurchase shares is restricted should we not pay dividends on preferred shares issued under the SBLF program.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Regulatory agencies measure capital adequacy within a framework that makes capital requirements, in part, dependent on the risk inherent in the balance sheets of individual financial institutions.&#160; The Company and the Banks continue to exceed the regulatory requirements for Tier I, Tier I leverage and total risk-based capital ratios (see Note 13 to the Consolidated Financial Statements).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As described in the notes to the consolidated financial statements (Footnote 2 &#151; Acquisition Activities), the Company acquired First Financial Service Corporation (&#147;FFKY&#148;) on January&nbsp;1, 2015.&#160; The Company issued 792,392 of its common shares to FFKY shareholders as part of the acquisition while also issuing 1,120,950 of its common shares to private investors to further enhance its capital position.&#160; The issuance of its common shares and related acquisition will have a material impact the amount of regulatory capital and capital ratios of the Company and YCB.&#160; Management expects to exceed regulatory capital requirements on a consolidated basis and its subsidiary banks immediately after the merger and associated purchase accounting adjustments.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

The term loan represents the scheduled maturities of holding company debt.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
