<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 4 &#151; LOANS</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Troubled Debt Restructurings:</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Troubled debt restructurings (&#147;TDR&#148;) totaled $11.9 million and $10.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.&#160; Of the total TDRs, $4.1 million and $389,000 were on non-accrual as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.&#160; The Company did not have any commitments to lend additional amounts to customers with outstanding loans that are classified as TDRs as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The detail of outstanding TDRs by class and modification type as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 follows (in thousands):</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="96%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:96.66%;">

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.72%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the terms of certain loans were modified as troubled debt restructurings. The modification of the terms of such loans included one or a combination of the following: a reduction of the stated interest rate of the loan; an extension of the maturity date at a stated rate of interest lower than the current market rate for new debt with similar risk; or adjustment of scheduled loan payments from principal and interest to interest only.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In order to determine whether a borrower is experiencing financial difficulty, an evaluation is performed of the probability that the borrower will be in payment default on any of its debt in the foreseeable future without the modification. This evaluation is performed under the company&#146;s internal underwriting policy.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 4 &#151; LOANS</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Credit Quality Indicators:</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company categorizes loans into risk categories based on relevant information about the ability of borrowers to service their debt such as:&#160; current financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors.&#160; The Company analyzes loans individually by classifying the loans as to credit risk and groups these loans into categories called &#147;criticized&#148; and &#147;classified&#148; assets.&#160; The Company considers its criticized assets to be loans risk rated as Watch or Special Mention and its classified assets to be loans risk rated Substandard or Doubtful.&#160; On a monthly basis, the Company reviews its loans that are risk rated Watch, Special Mention, Substandard, or Doubtful to determine they are properly classified.&#160; In addition, the Company reviews loans rated as a &#147;pass&#148; that have exhibited signs that may require a classification change, such as past due greater than 30 days and other relevant information including:&#160; loan officer recommendations, knowledge of specific borrower circumstances, and receipt of borrower financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the following definitions for its criticized loan risk ratings:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Watch.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans classified as watch are not considered &#147;rated&#148; or &#147;classified&#148; for regulatory purposes, but are considered criticized assets which exhibit modest deterioration in financial performance or external threats.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Special Mention.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans classified as special mention exhibit potential weaknesses that deserve management&#146;s close attention.&#160; If left uncorrected, these potential weaknesses may result in deterioration of the repayment prospects for the loan, or in the Company&#146;s credit position at some future date.&#160; Economic or market conditions exist which may affect the borrower more severely than other companies in its industry.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the following definitions for its classified loan risk ratings:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Substandard.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans classified as substandard are characterized by having well defined financial weakness.&#160; Substandard loans are usually evidenced by chronic or emerging past due performance and serious deficiencies in the primary source of repayment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 45.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Doubtful.&#160; </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans classified as doubtful have a well-defined and documented financial weaknesses.&#160; They have all the weaknesses of a substandard loan with the additional characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values highly questionable and improbable.&#160; Generally, loans classified as doubtful are on non-accrual.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">86<a name="PB_86_075500_5796"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 7 &#151; SHORT-TERM BORROWINGS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Short-term borrowings consist of retail repurchase agreements representing overnight borrowings from deposit customers and federal funds purchased representing overnight borrowings from other financial institutions.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 8 &#151; OTHER BORROWINGS </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal Home Loan Bank</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) advances had weighted average rates of 0.79% and 1.13% at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.&#160; The advances were collateralized by $372.0 million and $341.2 million of first mortgage and commercial real estate loans under a blanket lien arrangement and certain available for sale securities at year-end 2014 and 2013.&#160; Based on this collateral and the Company&#146;s holdings of FHLB stock, the Company is eligible to borrow an additional $61.4 million at year-end 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There is a substantial penalty if the Company prepays the advances before the contractual maturities.&#160; The Company did not recognize penalties on prepayment of FHLB advances during 2014, 2013, and 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Term Loan</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a term loan for $10.0 million from an unaffiliated institution.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The loan bears an interest rate of 5.35% and is payable in quarterly principal installments of $500,000 plus accrued interest with a final maturity of January&nbsp;2, 2020.&#160; The Company pledged the stock of both its subsidiary banks, Your Community Bank and The Scott County State Bank, as collateral.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subordinated Debentures</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;15, 2006, a trust formed by the Company, Community Bank Shares (IN) Statutory Trust II (Trust II), issued $10.0 million of floating rate trust preferred securities as part of a pooled offering of such securities.&#160; On June&nbsp;17, 2004, a trust formed by the Company, Community Bank Shares (IN) Statutory Trust I (Trust I), issued $7.0 million of floating rate trust preferred securities as part of a pooled offering of such securities.&#160; The Company issued subordinated debentures to Trusts I and II in exchange for the proceeds of each offering; the debentures and related debt issuance costs represent the sole assets of Trusts I and II.&#160; The Company is not considered the primary beneficiary of the Trusts (variable interest entity), therefore the trusts are not consolidated in the Company&#146;s financial statements, but rather the subordinated debentures are shown as a liability.&#160; Distributions on the trust preferred securities are payable quarterly in arrears at the annual rate (adjusted quarterly) of three-month LIBOR plus 1.70% (1.94% as of the last adjustment) for Trust II and three-month LIBOR plus 2.65% (2.89% as of the last adjustment) for Trust I and are included in interest expense.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The maturity dates of the subordinated debentures are June&nbsp;15, 2036 for Trust II and June&nbsp;17, 2034 for Trust I. The subordinated debentures may be redeemed by the Company, in whole or in part, at any distribution payment date at the redemption price. The subordinated debentures have variable rates, adjusted quarterly, which are identical to the trust preferred securities.&#160; In addition, the subordinated debentures are redeemable in whole or in part from time to time, upon the occurrence of specific events defined within the trust debenture.&#160; The Company has the option to defer interest payments on the subordinated debt from time to time for a period not to exceed five consecutive years.&#160; Should interest payments be deferred, the Company is restricted from paying dividends until all deferred payments have been made.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subordinated debentures are considered as Tier&nbsp;I capital for the Company under current regulatory guidelines.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">90<a name="PB_90_080841_141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 9 &#151; BENEFIT PLANS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Defined Benefit Plans</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The Company sponsors a defined benefit pension plan.&#160; The benefits are based on years of service and the employees&#146; highest average of total compensation for five consecutive years of employment.&#160; In 1997, the plan was amended such that there can be no new participants or increases in benefits to the participants.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A reconciliation of the projected benefit obligation and the value of plan assets follow.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:3.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 9 &#151; BENEFIT PLANS</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The investment policy of the pension plan prohibits investments in:&#160; fixed income securities not denominated in U.S. Dollars or Eurodollars, venture capital, guaranteed insurance contracts, commodities, precious metals or gems, derivatives, short-selling and other hedging strategies, or any other non-traditional asset.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term return is based on a periodic review and modeling of the plan&#146;s asset allocation and liability structure over a long-term horizon.&#160; Expectations of returns on each asset class are the most important of the assumptions used in the review and modeling and are based on reviews of historical data.&#160; The expected long-term rate of return on assets was selected from within the reasonable&#160; range of rates determined by (a)&nbsp;historical real returns, net of inflation, for the asset classes covered by the investment policy, and (b)&nbsp;projections of inflation over the long-term period during which benefit are payable to plan participants.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair Value of Plan Assets:</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. Also establishes a fair value hierarchy which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company used the following methods and significant assumptions to estimate the fair value of each type of financial instrument:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity Mutual Funds</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The fair values for equity mutual funds are determined by quoted market prices (Level 1).&#160; The Company does not modify or apply assumptions to the quoted market prices.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Money Market Mutual Funds</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The fair values for money market mutual funds are determined by quoted market prices (Level 1).&#160; The Company does not modify or apply assumptions to the quoted market prices.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">93<a name="PB_93_082751_5335"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 10 &#151; STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION PLANS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has three share based compensation plans as described below.&#160; Total compensation cost that has been charged against income for those plans was $603,000, $479,000, and $362,000 for 2014, 2013, and 2012.&#160; The total income tax benefit was $205,000, $163,000, and $123,000 for the respective periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock Options</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The Company&#146;s stock option plan provides for the granting of both incentive and nonqualified stock options and other share based awards, including restricted stock and deferred stock units, for up to 400,000 shares of common stock at exercise prices not less than the fair market value of the common stock on the date of grant and expiration dates of up to ten years.&#160; Terms of the options are determined by the Board of Directors at the date of grant and generally vest over periods of three to four years.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the plan allows for additional option and share-based award grants of up to 56,059 shares.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes model.&#160; Expected volatilities are based on historical volatilities of the Company&#146;s common stock. &#160;The Company uses historical data to estimate option exercise and post-vesting termination behavior.&#160; The expected term of options granted is based on historical data and represents the period of time that options granted are expected to be outstanding, which takes into account that the options are not transferable.&#160; The risk-free interest rate for the expected term of the option is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company did not grant options during 2014, 2013, or 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of the activity in the stock option plan for 2014 follows:</font></p>

The intrinsic value of stock options exercised during 2014 was $52,000.&#160; There were no options exercised or granted for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, and 2012.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, all outstanding stock options had vested and there was no remaining compensation cost to be recognized.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 10 &#151; STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION PLANS</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Performance Units Awards</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The Company may grant performance unit awards to employees for up to 275,000 shares of common stock.&#160; The level of performance shares eventually distributed is contingent upon the achievement of specific performance criteria within a specified award period set at the grant date.&#160; The Company estimates the progress toward achieving these objectives when estimating the number of awards expected to vest and correspondingly, periodic compensation expense.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The compensation cost attributable to these restricted performance units awards is based on both the fair market value of the shares at the grant date and the Company&#146;s stock price at the end of a reporting cycle.&#160; Thirty-five percent of the total award will be paid in cash and is therefore classified as a liability, with total compensation cost changing as the Company&#146;s stock price changes.&#160; The remaining sixty-five percent is classified as an equity award; total compensation cost is based on the fair market value of sixty-five percent of the total award on the date of grant.&#160; The compensation expense is recognized over the specified performance period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, there were no outstanding units granted under the Plan.&#160; There were no units outstanding during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012.&#160; There were no modifications or cash paid to settle performance unit awards during the three year period ending December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted Share Awards</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period of the awards based on the fair value of the stock at issue date.&#160; The fair value of the stock was determined using the market value of the Company&#146;s stock on the grant date.&#160; The restricted shares have vesting periods ranging from 18 days to three years from the anniversary of the grant date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:3.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of changes in the Company&#146;s nonvested shares for the year follows:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 11&#151; INCOME TAXES</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> (Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has no unrecognized tax benefits as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 and there is no expected change for unrecognized tax benefits over the next twelve months.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company did not record any amounts of interest and penalties in the income statement for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012 and did not have an amount accrued for interest and penalties at December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and its subsidiaries are subject to U.S. federal income tax as well as income tax of the states of Indiana and Kentucky. The Company is no longer subject to examination by taxing authorities for years before 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 12 &#151; PREFERRED STOCK</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;15, 2011, the Company entered into a security purchase agreement with the United States Department of the Treasury (&#147;Treasury&#148;) as part of its Small Business Lending Fund program, pursuant to which the Company sold 28,000 of its Senior Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series&nbsp;B (&#147;SBLF Preferred Stock&#148;) to the Treasury for a purchase price of $28,000,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The SBLF Preferred Stock qualifies as Tier 1 capital and will accrue non-cumulative dividends, payable quarterly, on each January&nbsp;1, April&nbsp;1, July&nbsp;1 and October&nbsp;1.&nbsp;&nbsp;The dividend rate, as a percentage of the liquidation amount, is fixed at 1.57% through the fourth quarter of 2015.&#160; If the SBLF Preferred Stock remains outstanding past 2015, the dividend rate will be fixed at 9%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such dividends are not cumulative, but the Company may only declare and pay dividends on its common stock (or any other equity securities junior to the SBLF Preferred Stock) if it has declared and paid dividends for the current dividend period on the SBLF Preferred Stock, and will be subject to other restrictions on its ability to repurchase or redeem other securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Holders of the SBLF Preferred Stock have the right to vote as a separate class on certain matters relating to the rights of holders of SBLF Preferred Stock and on certain corporate transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Except with respect to such matters and, if applicable, the election of the additional directors described below, the SBLF Preferred Stock does not have voting rights.&nbsp;&nbsp;If (i)&nbsp;the Company has not timely declared and paid dividends on the SBLF Preferred Stock for six dividend periods or more, whether or not consecutive, and (ii)&nbsp;shares of SBLF Preferred Stock with an aggregate liquidation preference of at least $25,000,000 are still outstanding, the Treasury (or any successor holder of SBLF Preferred Stock) may elect two additional directors to the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the event that the Company misses five dividend payments, whether or not consecutive, the holder of the SBLF Preferred Stock will have the right, but not the obligation, to appoint a representative as an observer on the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 12 &#151; PREFERRED STOCK </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company may redeem the shares of SBLF Preferred Stock, in whole or in part, at any time at a redemption price equal to the sum of the liquidation amount per share ($1,000 per share) and the per-share amount of any unpaid dividends for the then-current period, subject to any required prior approval by the Company&#146;s primary federal banking regulator. The terms of the SBLF Preferred Stock impose limits on the ability of the Company to pay dividends and repurchase shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of the SBLF Preferred Stock, no repurchases may be effected, and no dividends may be declared or paid on preferred shares ranking pari passu with the SBLF Preferred Stock, junior preferred shares, or other junior securities (including the common stock) during the current quarter and for the next three quarters following the failure to declare and pay dividends on the SBLF Preferred Stock, except that, in any such quarter in which the dividend is paid, dividend payments on shares ranking pari passu may be paid to the extent necessary to avoid any resulting material covenant breach.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the SBLF Preferred Stock, the Company may only declare and pay a dividend on the common stock or other stock junior to the SBLF Preferred Stock, or repurchase shares of any such class or series of stock, if, after payment of such dividend, the dollar amount of the Company&#146;s Tier 1 Capital would be at least 90% of the&nbsp;Tier 1 Capital of the Company as of September&nbsp;15, 2011, excluding any subsequent net charge-offs and any redemption of the SBLF Preferred Stock (the &#147;Tier 1 Dividend Threshold&#148;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning on the first day of the eleventh dividend period, the amount of the Tier 1 Dividend Threshold will be reduced by 10% for each one percent increase in QSBL from the baseline level through the ninth dividend period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 13 &#151; CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS AND RESTRICTIONS ON DIVIDENDS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Banks and bank holding companies are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies.&#160; Capital adequacy guidelines and, additionally for banks, prompt corrective action regulations involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices.&#160; Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators.&#160; Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prompt corrective action regulations provide five classifications:&#160; well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are not used to represent overall financial condition.&#160; If adequately capitalized, regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits.&#160; If undercapitalized, capital distributions are limited, as is asset growth and expansion, and capital restoration plans are required.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the most recent regulatory notifications categorized YCB and SCSB as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.&#160; There are no considerations or events since December&nbsp;31, 2014 that management believes have changed the institution&#146;s classification as well capitalized.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">100<a name="PB_100_081058_5335"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 13 &#151; CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS AND RESTRICTIONS ON DIVIDENDS </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividend Restrictions</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The Company&#146;s principal source of funds for dividend payments is dividends received from the Banks.&#160; Banking regulations limit the amount of dividends that may be paid without prior approval of regulatory agencies.&#160; Under these regulations, the amount of dividends that may be paid in any calendar year is limited to the current year&#146;s retained net profits, combined with the retained net profits of the preceding two years, subject to the capital requirements described above.&#160; In 2015, YCB could declare dividends of $2.5 million plus 2015 earnings without prior regulatory approval while SCSB could not declare dividends without prior approval.&#160; In addition, the Company has limitations on dividends it can pay to common shareholders as more fully described in Note 12 &#151; Preferred Stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 14 &#151; OFF-BALANCE-SHEET ACTIVITIES</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Some financial instruments, such as commitments to make loans for the Company&#146;s portfolio, credit lines and letters of credit, are issued to meet customer-financing needs.&#160; These are agreements to provide credit or to support the credit of others, as long as conditions established in the contract are met, and usually have expiration dates.&#160; Commitments may expire without being used.&#160; Off-balance-sheet risk to credit loss exists up to the face amount of these instruments, although material losses are not anticipated.&#160; The same credit policies are used to make such commitments as are used for loans, including obtaining collateral at exercise of the commitment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The contractual amount of financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk was as follows at year-end.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15 &#151; FAIR VALUE</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.&#160; There are three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair values:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 1</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; Quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets that the entity has the ability to access as of the measurement date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 2</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; Significant other observable inputs other than Level 1 prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities, quoted prices in markets that are not active, and other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 3</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; Significant unobservable inputs that reflect a company&#146;s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company used the following methods and significant assumptions to estimate the fair value:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; The fair values of securities available for sale are determined by obtaining quoted prices on nationally recognized securities exchanges (Level 1 inputs) or matrix pricing, which is a mathematical technique used widely in the industry to value debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#146; relationship to other benchmark quoted securities (Level 2 inputs). In instances where broker quotes are used, these quotes are obtained from market makers or broker-dealers recognized to be market participants. These valuation methods are classified as Level 2 in the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impaired Loans</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">:&#160; Impaired loans are evaluated at the time the loan is identified as impaired and are recorded at the lower of the carrying amount of the loan or the fair value of the underlying collateral less costs to sell.&#160; For collateral dependent loans, the fair value of real estate is primarily determined based on appraisals by qualified licensed appraisers.&#160; These appraisals may use a single valuation approach or a combination depending on the type of collateral, including the comparable sales or income capitalization approach.&#160; The appraisals are discounted to reflect management&#146;s estimate of the fair value of the collateral given the current circumstances and condition of the collateral including the market for the particular collateral and management&#146;s experience with similar types of collateral.&#160; Impaired loans are evaluated quarterly for additional impairment.&#160; Fair value of impaired loans is classified as Level 3 in the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreclosed and Repossessed Assets:</font></u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Foreclosed and repossessed assets are initially recorded at fair value less estimated costs to sell when acquired.&#160; The fair value of foreclosed and repossessed assets is primarily determined based on appraisals by qualified licensed appraisers whose qualifications have been reviewed by the Company.&#160; The appraisals are discounted to reflect management&#146;s estimate of the fair value of the collateral given the current circumstances of the collateral and reduced by management&#146;s estimate of costs to dispose of the asset.&#160; Also, management reviews the assumptions included in the appraisals and makes adjustments where circumstances warrant, such as recent experience with similar assets.&#160; Fair value of foreclosed and repossessed assets is classified as Level 3 in the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">103<a name="PB_103_082220_3020"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15 &#151; FAIR VALUE </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company measures for impairment using the fair value of the collateral less costs to sell for collateral-dependent loans.&#160; The Company&#146;s impaired loans totaled $15.0 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, which included collateral-dependent loans with a carrying value of $4.1 million.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company&#146;s collateral dependent loans had a valuation allowance of $1.1 million, resulting in an additional provision for loan losses of $760,000 during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The Company&#146;s impaired loans totaled $18.4 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013, which included collateral-dependent loans with a carrying value of $8.0 million.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2013, the Company&#146;s collateral dependent loans had a valuation allowance of $1.7 million, resulting in an additional provision for loan losses of $3.3 million during the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company evaluates the fair value of foreclosed assets at the time they are transferred from loans and on a quarterly basis thereafter. &#160;During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the Company recognized charges of $251,000 and $138,000 to write down foreclosed assets to their fair value.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">106<a name="PB_106_082537_5796"></a></font></p>

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The methods and assumptions used to estimate fair value are described as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The methods and assumptions, not previously presented, used to estimate fair values are described as follows:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(a)&nbsp;Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values and are classified as Level 1.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(b)&nbsp;FHLB and FRB Stock</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is not practical to determine the fair value of FHLB and FRB stock due to restrictions placed on transferability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(c)&nbsp;Loans</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair values of loans, excluding loans held for sale, are estimated as follows:&#160; For variable rate loans that reprice frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values resulting in a Level 3 classification. Fair values for other loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers of similar credit quality resulting in a Level 3 classification.&#160; Impaired loans are valued at the lower of cost or fair value as described previously. The methods utilized to estimate the fair value of loans do not necessarily represent an exit price.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">110<a name="PB_110_083118_141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">COMMUNITY BANK SHARES OF INDIANA,&nbsp;INC.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTE 15 &#151; FAIR VALUE </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of loans held for sale is estimated based upon binding contracts and quotes from third party investors resulting in a Level 2 classification.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(e)&nbsp;Deposits</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value disclosed for demand deposits are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date resulting in a Level 2 classification. Fair values for fixed rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flows calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits resulting in a Level 2 classification.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(f)&nbsp;Other Borrowings</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values of the Company&#146;s long-term borrowings are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the current borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements resulting in a Level 2 classification.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair values of the Company&#146;s Subordinated Debentures are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the current borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements resulting in a Level 3 classification.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(g)&nbsp;Accrued Interest Receivable/Payable</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair value resulting in a Level 2 or Level 3 classification depending upon the classification of the associated asset or liability.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">(i)&nbsp;Off-balance Sheet Instruments</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair values for off-balance sheet, credit-related financial instruments are based on fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#146; credit standing. The fair value of commitments is not material.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">111<a name="PB_111_083148_7608"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Company management, including the Chief Executive Officer (serving as the principal executive officer) and Chief Financial Officer (serving as the principal financial officer), have conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures pursuant to Securities Exchange Act of 1934 Rule&nbsp;13a-15. Based on that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer concluded that the disclosure controls and procedures are effective in timely alerting them to material information required to be included in this report.&#160; There has been no change in the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the Company&#146;s most recent fiscal quarter that has materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>
